name: Jordan Brock
short: Leads brand and commercial strategy, and the relationships with artists, labels and rights holders.
full: Jordan's career spans enterprise technology at Dell and Rackspace, helping grow The Happy Co. past $100 million in annual revenue under its publicly traded parent company, and working alongside New York Times bestselling author Shawn Achor at GoodThink.

As an entrepreneur he has built products that were supposed to be impossible: one of the first commercially viable zero-net-carb breads that actually tasted and behaved like bread, early perceptual sugar technology, and Tipsy Tabs, a dissolvable tablet designed to rethink the economics of social drinks.

Every one of them rested on the same conviction, that an impossible trade-off is usually just an unsolved problem. lyrical is that conviction applied to music: an artist should never have to choose between global reach and artistic identity.

name: Henry McMahon
short: Builds the production system: the translation, the voice work, and the pipeline that turns a finished master into a release-ready version.
full: A Mechatronics Engineering graduate from Monash University in Melbourne, Henry leads engineering and is building the technology that powers the platform.

His work turns an ambitious idea into infrastructure: a system capable of serving artists and rights holders around the world, and of holding a standard high enough that a label will put its name on the result.
